title: Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2026)
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard processes for annual budgeting, rolling forecasting, procurement approvals, contract lifecycle management, and core revenue recognition and billing rules. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and stakeholders across Product and Engineering who participate in resource planning, vendor selection, contracting, or revenue reporting.

Scope

- Applies to all corporate and product-line budgets, capital expenditure (CapEx) requests, procurement of third-party services (software, cloud, consulting, hardware), and customer/partner contract intake processed by the Finance & Legal teams.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific security or compliance questionnaires (see security-and-compliance pages).

Key Principles

1. Transparency: budgets and forecasts must be auditable and reconcilable to GL accounts.
2. Control: procurement and contracting flow through documented approval gates.
3. Accuracy: revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles and local GAAP; billing follows contract terms and platform usage logs.
4. Efficiency: standard templates, thresholds, and self-serve tools wherever possible.

Ownership and Roles

- Finance (Budgeting & Forecasting): overall owner of annual budget, rolling forecast, and financial consolidation.
- Legal: owner of contract templates, risk reviews, and final sign-off for non-routine terms.
- Procurement: owner of vendor onboarding, vendor risk checks, and PO issuance.
- Product/Engineering Managers: requesters of budget and owners of budget-line usage and forecast inputs.
- Sales & RevOps: owners of contract negotiation with customers and handing off signed contracts to billing.

Annual Budgeting Process (Cadence and Steps)

1. Planning Timeline
   1.1. Budget kickoff: early October \u2014 Finance issues templates and assumptions for next fiscal year.
   1.2. Draft submissions by departments: due mid-November.
   1.3. Consolidation and leadership review: December.
   1.4. Board submission and approval: January.

2. Template and Inputs
   - Use the official budget workbook (Finance -> Shared Drive). Required sheets: revenue model, headcount plan, OPEX by category, CapEx requests, and 3-year rolling forecast.
   - Assumptions must include model mix (hosted/dedicated/private), pricing assumptions, expected RFPs, and large one-time expenditures.

3. Approval Thresholds
   - Department-level approves budgets up to $500k incremental OPEX; Finance & CFO review above.
   - CapEx > $250k requires CFO and CEO sign-off.

Rolling Forecast Process

- Rolling 12-month forecast is updated monthly by Finance, with key inputs from GTM, Product, and Engineering.
- Forecast tiers: best case, base case (required), downside case.
- Material variance triggers: >10% revenue detraction or >15% cost overrun vs. prior month forecast \u2014 requires leadership review and variance RCA.

Procurement Procedures (Vendor Onboarding and Purchase Requests)

1. Initiation
   - Requester files a Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement system with: business justification, estimated total cost, vendor legal entity, SOW (if applicable), and required delivery dates.

2. Vendor Risk and Compliance Checks
   - Procurement runs vendor due diligence: tax W-9/W-8, AML screen, security questionnaire if vendor touches customer data.
   - If vendor handles customer data or is critical infra, procurement routes vendor to Security & Compliance for a SOC2/ISO review.

3. Approvals (Standard thresholds)
   - <= $10k: Manager approval.
   - $10k - $100k: Department head + Procurement.
   - $100k - $500k: Finance lead + Procurement + Legal notification.
   - > $500k: CFO + Legal + Procurement mandatory review; Procurement issues RFP where appropriate.

4. Purchase Orders and Invoicing
   - Procurement issues PO once approvals obtained. POs are binding only when signed by Procurement or Finance. Invoices must reference PO number for automated matching.

5. Preferred Vendors and Contracts
   - Use preferred vendor list where feasible (stored in procurement system). For cloud providers, reference standard cloud agreements vetted by Legal.

Contracts and Legal Process (Lifecycle)

1. Contract Intake
   - All inbound and outbound contracts must be submitted to Legal via the contract intake form. Include required commercial terms, SOW, requested signature authority, and redlines.

2. Contract Review Triage
   - Triage categories: Standard (template-friendly), Non-standard (requires negotiation), High-risk (data residency, IP, indemnity, revenue share).

3. Escalation and Approvals
   - Standard templates: Legal approves and GC sign-off may be delegated to Senior Counsel for values up to $250k or standard SaaS subscriptions.
   - Non-standard/high-risk: Legal + Head of Finance + CTO (if technical risk) must approve. Any modification to indemnity, limitation of liability, IP assignment, or data residency requires GC approval.

4. Signature Authority
   - Delegated signature authority matrix: 
     - Sales Director: execute standard customer agreements up to $500k ARR (per signed S-schedule).
     - VP Finance / CFO: execute commercial agreements up to $2M.
     - CEO: > $2M or any material strategic partnership.

5. Contract Repository
   - All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the contract repository (DocuSign + ContractDB) within 48 hours. Procurement and RevOps will not process invoices or revenue recognition until contracts are in the repository.

Procurement and Contract Playbook: Common Scenarios

- Emergency Purchase (hardware failure or critical vendor outage): Manager approval + Procurement notified ASAP; retrospective approvals required within 48 hours.
- Professional Services (SOW-based): SOW must include milestones, acceptance criteria, and invoicing schedule. Retainer agreements must be capped and approved by Finance.

Revenue Recognition and Billing Policies (Summary)

1. Revenue Recognition Principles
   - Redwood follows ASC 606 (or applicable local GAAP): identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate transaction price, recognize revenue as obligations are satisfied.
   - Standalone unit prices are based on list prices adjusted for observable discounts. Material variable consideration is assessed and constrained until resolvable.

2. Common Revenue Scenarios
   - Hosted API usage (consumption): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (over time) based on metered tokens/embeddings. Monthly invoicing with usage report.
   - Dedicated Reserved Capacity (committed): Recognize ratably over the committed term unless performance obligations indicate a different pattern. Upfront prepaid variants are deferred and amortized.
   - Private Deployment/License + Services: License components recognized per license treatment (may be at a point in time) and services (implementation/support) recognized over service delivery period.

3. Billing Rules and Invoice Processing
   - Billing frequency by product: Hosted API \u2014 monthly in arrears; Dedicated \u2014 monthly/quarterly per contract; Private \u2014 milestone-based and/or monthly support fees.
   - Invoicing data must include contract ID, billing period, line-level usage detail, taxes, PO number (if provided), and payment instructions.
   - Disputed invoices: Sales/RevOps must log dispute within 10 business days; payment holds require Finance/RevOps approval.

4. Deferred Revenue and Revenue Deferral Matrix
   - Desktop table (text format):

     | Scenario                         | Recognize When                    | Deferral Treatment                | Owner    |
     |----------------------------------|------------------------------------|----------------------------------|----------|
     | Prepaid dedicated capacity        | Over service term                  | Defer to deferred revenue GL     | RevOps   |
     | Prepaid training/service package | When service milestones complete   | Partially defer until milestone  | Finance  |
     | Usage-based hosted API           | As usage occurs                    | N/A                              | RevOps   |

5. Revenue Cutover and Close Activities
   - Close checklist for month end: billing run completed, invoices issued, usage reconciliation (platform logs vs billing), deferred revenue schedules updated, and journal entries prepared for revenue recognized.

Controls, Reporting, and Audit Requirements

- Access Controls: Billing and contract systems follow RBAC. Only authorized roles can create invoices or modify contracts.
- Audit Trail: All contract approvals, PO issuance, and invoice matches must be traceable in the systems. Retain source documents for 7 years.
- Management Reporting: Monthly P&L by product line, deferred revenue roll-forward, and variance analysis against forecast.

Escalation and Exception Handling

- Exceptions to thresholds: documented exceptions require written justification and approval from CFO and GC.
- Significant contract disputes or potential revenue restatements: immediate notification to Finance leadership and Legal; may trigger audit committee notification.

Appendices

A. Approval Matrix (Quick Reference)
   - Purchase <= $10k: Manager.
   - $10k - $100k: Dept head + Procurement.
   - $100k - $500k: Finance + Procurement + notify Legal.
   - > $500k: CFO + Legal + Procurement.

B. Standard Contract Clauses to Avoid or Escalate
   - Unlimited indemnity or uncapped consequential damages.
   - Broad IP assignment requests without product team review.
   - Data residency/localization commitments without infra feasibility sign-off.

C. Templates and Tools (location)
   - Budget workbook: Finance -> Shared Drive -> FY Budgets.
   - Contract templates: Legal -> Confluence -> Contract Templates.
   - Procurement system: Procurement -> Ariba/JAGGAER (internal link).
   - Billing & RevRec: RevOps -> Billing Portal + Finance -> NetSuite accounting.

D. Contact List

   - Procurement Lead: Arjun Patel (arjun.patel@redwood.example.com).
   - Legal (Contracts): Emily Zhao, Senior Counsel (emily.zhao@redwood.example.com).
